units.rhetorical_move: opens on the material, then turns to the harm
units.function: grant the convenience before the ocean damage

original_instantiations: A handy cheap material is granted, and only then does the ocean harm arrive.
The opening lets the use stand before it names the damage.

units.source_excerpt: Plastic is everywhere. Due to its convenience and low cost, plastic is used in many settings before it is quickly disposed of. Unfortunately, much of this plastic makes its way into our oceans, where it wreaks havoc
units.reusable_pattern: Grant the convenience in one sentence and turn with the damage in the next.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the opening praise as the paper's recommendation

units.rhetorical_move: names the animal as the health metric
units.function: choose one population to stand for the ocean

original_instantiations: One animal count is asked to stand in for the whole marine state.
The metric is a future population, not a waste total.

units.source_excerpt: In this paper, we consider predicted future seabird populations as a metric for evaluating the future effect of our current plastic production.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the proxy in the sentence that says what the paper will judge.
prohibited_generalizations: do not export this animal to papers that never mention it

units.rhetorical_move: states the two endangered years
units.function: give the no-change forecast as two years

original_instantiations: The no-change path is reported as two later years, one worse than the other.
A forecast can land as a pair of dated thresholds.

units.source_excerpt: we predict that, if global plastic production continues at its current pace, seabirds will become endangered by the year 2056 and will become critically endangered by 2062.
units.reusable_pattern: Report the unchanged path as the year a line is crossed and the year a worse line is crossed.
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse these years outside this projection

units.rhetorical_move: picks the policy by the smallest cost
units.function: end on the cut that still lets the animals recover

original_instantiations: The chosen plan is a steady yearly cut down to a named remaining stock.
Recovery and the smallest cost are claimed in the same sentence.

units.source_excerpt: an appropriate global policy would be to reduce accumulated plastic by a constant amount each year until the remaining volume of plastic is less than 3,750 million metric tons. This policy will allow the seabird population to recover while imposing the minimum economic cost to society.
units.reusable_pattern: Close the summary by naming the cut, the remaining stock, and the cost claim together.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the remaining stock as computed on this page

units.rhetorical_move: starts the history, then the unnoticed benefit
units.function: put a date on the waste and then the people who miss it

original_instantiations: A start date is given, then the people who still enjoy the product.
The harm is reserved for the animals after the human benefit.

units.source_excerpt: Since the large scale production of single-use disposable plastics began in the 1950s, there has been an accumulation of plastic waste in the environment, particularly our oceans [1]. Although the accumulation of this plastic pollution has gone unnoticed by many who enjoy the benefits
units.reusable_pattern: Date the industry, then concede that the users have not noticed.
reusable_elements: a concession that users do not notice
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the citation as this paper's own measurement

units.rhetorical_move: gives the yearly ocean range
units.function: put one borrowed interval behind the accumulation

original_instantiations: The yearly ocean load is borrowed as a range, not a point.
An estimate can stay inside the citation's interval.

units.source_excerpt: It is estimated that 4-12 million metric tons of plastic waste end up in the ocean every year [2].
units.reusable_pattern: Borrow the yearly load as a range with the citation attached.
prohibited_generalizations: do not collapse the range to one number

units.rhetorical_move: says the waste stays unless people act
units.function: make permanence the reason a policy is needed

original_instantiations: Slow decay is used to say the stock stays unless someone removes it.
Permanence is the bridge from a stock to a policy.

units.source_excerpt: plastic degrades at a very slow rate, so plastic that is added to the ocean stays in the ocean in perpetuity if no human action is taken [4].
units.reusable_pattern: Tie slow decay to permanence, and permanence to the need for action.
prohibited_generalizations: do not read perpetuity as a measured half-life

units.rhetorical_move: lists the four jobs as bullets
units.function: turn the aim into a numbered set of jobs

original_instantiations: The aim is unpacked into four jobs, each a bullet.
A report can preview the work as a list rather than a narrative.

units.source_excerpt: To achieve this objective, we do the following:
units.reusable_pattern: Announce the objective and then let the bullets carry the jobs.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the bullets as results

units.rhetorical_move: labels an assumption and stops
units.function: set the proxy off with an assumption label

original_instantiations: The proxy is announced as a labeled assumption, not slipped into a method sentence.
A label can do the work of a hedge.

units.source_excerpt: Assumption: Seabird population S(t) is a useful proxy for estimating global marine environmental health at time t.
units.reusable_pattern: Put the word Assumption in front of the sentence that chooses the proxy.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat a labeled assumption as a tested result

units.rhetorical_move: defends the proxy, then the animal's own worth
units.function: give the literature reason and then a second reason

original_instantiations: The proxy is defended twice: it tracks the ocean, and the animal matters on its own.
A remark can stack a literature reason on a value reason.

units.source_excerpt: Seabirds have been shown to be a reliable bioindicator of the state of the marine environment for a variety of reasons including their wide-ranging area of habitation and their rapid response to changes in their environment [5].
units.reusable_pattern: Defend a proxy with the range it covers and the speed of its response.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the citation when reusing the defense

units.rhetorical_move: introduces the balance as a differential equation
units.function: name the equation before the line

original_instantiations: The balance is announced as a differential equation and then written.
A short lead-in can hand the reader to the line.

units.source_excerpt: We can model the seabird population S with the following differential equation:
units.reusable_pattern: Announce the equation in a short sentence and let the line follow.
prohibited_generalizations: do not narrate the algebra inside the lead-in

units.rhetorical_move: picks the reference bird and the reason
units.function: choose one species because it is called average

original_instantiations: One species is chosen and called representative of the average bird.
The reason is breeding, survival, and feeding, given as a because-clause.

units.source_excerpt: We chose the razorbill as our reference seabird because breeding and survival rates and feeding behaviors are representative of the average seabird.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the reference species and the trait that makes it stand for the group.
prohibited_generalizations: do not swap in a different animal without the trait

units.rhetorical_move: states a rate and the product that is said to produce it
units.function: give the decimal and the product in one bullet

original_instantiations: A rate is printed as a decimal and then as a product of two cited figures.
The bullet holds both the value and the claimed arithmetic.

units.source_excerpt: b = 0.326, which represents the number of births per seabird. This is obtained by multiplying the productivity of each pair of seabirds (0.895) by the fraction seabirds that are at breeding age (approximately 8/13)
units.reusable_pattern: State the decimal, then the product that is supposed to have produced it.
reusable_elements: the product claimed to equal it
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the product and the decimal as the same number unless they match

units.rhetorical_move: states the plastic death rate and the quotient
units.function: give the decimal and the three-factor quotient together

original_instantiations: A death rate is printed as a decimal and then as a quotient of two shares over a stock.
The same bullet holds the value and the claimed division.

units.source_excerpt: dp = 8.395e-06, which is the number of seabird deaths due to plastic per seabird per million metric tons of cumulative plastic produced.
units.reusable_pattern: State the small rate, then the quotient the paper says produced it.
reusable_elements: the quotient claimed to equal it
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the quotient and the decimal as the same number unless they match

units.rhetorical_move: sets the reduction to zero at the start
units.function: make activation a labeled assumption with an arrow

original_instantiations: The start of a policy is a labeled line: no reduction yet, so the stock is the trend.
An arrow does the work of a therefore.

units.source_excerpt: Assumption: On time of policy activation (Ta), countries do not contribute to reducing accumulated global levels of plastic, i.e.:
units.reusable_pattern: Label the start condition, then let the arrow line say what follows.
prohibited_generalizations: do not start the reduction before the labeled year

units.rhetorical_move: says the policy is the trend minus the reduction
units.function: define the after-branch in a remark before the cases

original_instantiations: The remark says the later branch in words, and the cases come after.
A therefore can land before the displayed cases.

units.source_excerpt: After Ta, when plastic reduction plan Pr has come into effect, we express Ppolicy as Ptrend with the cumulative reduction of plastic defined in Pr, or Ppolicy = Ptrend − Pr.
units.reusable_pattern: Say the later branch in words, with the symbols, before the piecewise line.
prohibited_generalizations: do not apply the difference before the start year

units.rhetorical_move: says what countries will accept
units.function: define the cost by the two things a country dislikes

original_instantiations: Acceptance is assumed to rise when the cut is small and the pace is gentle.
Two dislikes are numbered inside the assumption.

units.source_excerpt: Assumption: Countries will more readily accept a policy that minimizes (1) the quantity of cumulative saved plastic from the ocean and (2) the rate of decrease of their plastic production.
units.reusable_pattern: Number the two things the cost is about to add.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add a third penalty the assumption did not number

units.rhetorical_move: names hostility as the weight
units.function: gloss the symbol as a country's dislike of abrupt change

original_instantiations: The weight is glossed as hostility to a sharp year-to-year change.
A where-clause can name the feeling the symbol stands for.

units.source_excerpt: where λ is a constant that represents a country’s hostility to extreme changes in plastic production levels form year to year.
units.reusable_pattern: Gloss the weight as hostility to a sharp change, and keep the printed wording.
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent a number for the weight

units.rhetorical_move: treats countries as separate rational agents
units.function: say each country serves its own market, then the shared duty

original_instantiations: Each country is said to serve its own market, and the shared duty comes after however.
The turn is from private interest to a duty they ignore.

units.source_excerpt: In the absence of global policies, countries act as individual rational agents to produce the amount of plastic necessary to keep their local economies running at the optimal level.
units.reusable_pattern: Call the countries separate agents first, and bring in the shared duty afterwards.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the market claim as an estimated demand curve

units.section: 3 Predicting the Point of Irreversible Damage
units.rhetorical_move: asks the irreversible-damage question in italics
units.function: open the result with the question the section will answer

original_instantiations: The section opens by repeating the question it is about to answer.
Italics mark the question off from the method.

units.source_excerpt: In this section, we answer the question: If we do not change our current plastic production policies, when will the damage we cause to the environment reach an irreversible level?
units.reusable_pattern: Open a result by restating the question, then answer it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the question unanswered in the same section

units.section: 3 Predicting the Point of Irreversible Damage
units.rhetorical_move: prefers the quartic and says why
units.function: reject the other curve by a worse fit and by the integral

original_instantiations: The curve is chosen for a better fit and because the yearly series was one degree lower.
Two reasons are numbered, one statistical and one by integration.

units.source_excerpt: We use chose to use a quartic polynomial fit for two reasons. The first reason is that an exponential curve did not fit as well
units.reusable_pattern: Give two reasons for the degree, and keep the printed slip.
prohibited_generalizations: do not correct the printed slip when quoting the move

units.section: 3 Predicting the Point of Irreversible Damage
units.rhetorical_move: reads the peak and then the decline
units.function: narrate the figure as a rise and then a fall

original_instantiations: The path is said to rise at the start and to fall after a peak.
A figure reading can be a peak year plus a direction.

units.source_excerpt: Plotting Strend(t) for the years 1950 to 2150, we see that seabird population was increasing when plastic production first took off in the 1950s, but the population peaks around the year 2000 and has been in a steady decline since
units.reusable_pattern: Read a projection as an early rise, a peak, and a decline.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the peak year as a datum from a census

units.section: 3 Predicting the Point of Irreversible Damage
units.rhetorical_move: applies the two conservation thresholds
units.function: translate a count into a status and a year

original_instantiations: A borrowed status rule turns a projected count into a year.
The paper flags its own year as slightly late.

units.source_excerpt: According to the The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), a species is considered endangered if the population size is estimated to be fewer than 2,500 mature individuals
units.reusable_pattern: Cite the status rule, then the year the projection crosses it, and own the lateness.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the mature-individual hedge

units.rhetorical_move: rejects the no-cleanup plan
units.function: show two curves meeting at zero and call the plan useless

original_instantiations: Stopping production without removal is said to delay the fall and still end at zero.
The rejection is that the two curves meet.

units.source_excerpt: even the immediate termination of plastic production is not enough to save the sea birds, as shown in Figure 3.
units.reusable_pattern: Reject a plan by saying even its strongest form fails, and point at the figure.
prohibited_generalizations: do not compute a cost for a plan the section has just called useless

units.rhetorical_move: warns that the late rise should be read carefully
units.function: own the missing ceiling before the reader trusts the takeoff

original_instantiations: The late rise is flagged because the equation has no ceiling.
The caution is about large populations, not about the direction of recovery.

units.source_excerpt: One should note that the tail end behavior of predicted bird population should be interpreted with caution.
units.reusable_pattern: Warn about the far tail, and say which part of the claim still stands.
reusable_elements: a limit on what it shows
prohibited_generalizations: do not read the late takeoff as a census

units.rhetorical_move: says a leftover stock can still save the birds
units.function: drop the demand that every ton be removed

original_instantiations: Full removal is called unnecessary, and a leftover stock is allowed.
The turn is from the aggressive plan to a floor.

units.source_excerpt: we show that complete plastic cleanup is not a necessary condition to save the environment and that the environment is still able to recover even if some amount of plastic remains in the oceans.
units.reusable_pattern: Say the stricter plan is unnecessary, then the weaker plan that still works.
prohibited_generalizations: do not equate the leftover with zero

units.rhetorical_move: defines the share as a ratio of two flows
units.function: turn the global cut into a dimensionless factor

original_instantiations: The global cut is turned into a ratio so it can move across units.
A dimensionless factor is justified by the unit change it allows.

units.source_excerpt: To further quantify the overall shift of global plastic production, we define α to be the ratio
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce a ratio by the unit change it makes legal.
prohibited_generalizations: do not apply the ratio to a stock when it was defined on a flow

units.rhetorical_move: leaves the low producers alone
units.function: say who is capped and who is not

original_instantiations: Countries under the class mean are left alone, and only those above it are capped.
The rule is a split, not a uniform cut.

units.source_excerpt: If a country intends to produce plastic per capita at a level below x˜k, then this country should be left untouched by the global policy.
units.reusable_pattern: State the exemption first, then the cap for the countries above the line.
prohibited_generalizations: do not cap a country the sentence has just exempted

units.rhetorical_move: places one country above its class mean
units.function: use one country to show the cap will bind

original_instantiations: One rich country is placed above its class mean, so the cap binds.
A case can be a single comparison.

units.source_excerpt: The United States is one of 74 countries within the high income class (HI). It produces 1.2195e-7 Mt of plastic per capita per year, which is above x¯HI = 1.08e-7.
units.reusable_pattern: Place a country in its class, then compare its per-person figure with the class mean.
prohibited_generalizations: do not infer a national total from the per-person figure alone

units.rhetorical_move: converts a tiny mass into kilograms per person
units.function: finish a case by the kilograms one person must pick up

original_instantiations: A very small mass is converted into kilograms per person.
The case ends on a duty for one person, not a national total.

units.source_excerpt: each person in Somalia needs to pick up at least 0.1949 kg of plastic waste more than they produce by the end of 2020
units.reusable_pattern: End a country case by converting the factor into kilograms one person must remove.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the sign when the factor was negative

units.rhetorical_move: claims the metric is interpretable
units.function: say the ocean is too large and the bird count is the reduction

original_instantiations: Complexity is conceded, then one count is offered as the reduction.
Interpretability is the advantage named after the reduction.

units.source_excerpt: We managed to distill the complexity of evaluating the health of the environment into a single metric: seabird population.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede the size of the system, then name the one metric that replaces it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the metric captures every species

units.rhetorical_move: claims the cost captures both burden and resistance
units.function: split feasibility from willingness

original_instantiations: Total burden and resistance to change are separated, then joined in the minimum plan.
A strength can be two dependencies and the plan they pick.

units.source_excerpt: The dependency on total cost allows us to model the overall feasibility of the target plastic level set by the policy.
units.reusable_pattern: Separate the total burden from the resistance to a fast change.
prohibited_generalizations: do not merge the two into one unlabeled penalty

units.rhetorical_move: owns the missing ceiling
units.function: say the recovery path grows too fast because competition was left out

original_instantiations: The missing ceiling is owned, and the overstated recovery is the consequence.
A limit can name the term that was refused and the bias it causes.

units.source_excerpt: we chose not to introduce added complexity by including a carrying capacity in the seabird population model
units.reusable_pattern: Own the term that was left out and the direction in which the forecast then errs.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat the late takeoff as bounded

units.rhetorical_move: stops mid-heading and owns the unfinished timeline
units.function: admit the interval was a deadline, not an optimum

original_instantiations: A heading breaks off, and the next sentences admit the interval was not optimized.
Running out of time is given as the reason.

units.source_excerpt: We can. While our policy cost metric determines that a constant year-to-year reduction is the most adoptable policy, we have not fully defined every concrete detail
units.reusable_pattern: Leave the broken heading, and say which calculation the deadline replaced.
prohibited_generalizations: do not complete the heading

units.rhetorical_move: restates the year and the remaining stock
units.function: answer the opening question in two sentences

original_instantiations: The unchanged path gets a year, and the alternative gets a remaining stock.
The conclusion answers the question the introduction asked.

units.source_excerpt: we determined that if plastic consumption levels increase at their current rate, irreversible damage will be caused to the environment by the year 2056.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate the damage year, then the cut that avoids it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not introduce a new model in the conclusion

units.rhetorical_move: says an even split would burden some countries more
units.function: justify the income classes as a correction to an even split

original_instantiations: An even split is rejected because some countries would carry more than they can.
Income classes are the correction, not a new objective.

units.source_excerpt: Since evenly splitting economic costs across all countries may result in heavier burdens for certain countries, we stratify each country by income class
units.reusable_pattern: Reject the even split, then name the grouping that replaces it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the grouping equalizes income

units.rhetorical_move: addresses the council by name
units.function: open the memo with the addressee and the hard task

original_instantiations: The memo names the council and then the hard task.
There is no singular self-introduction.

units.source_excerpt: To the International Council of Plastic Waste Management (ICM):
units.reusable_pattern: Open by naming the council, then the task, with no self-introduction.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add a singular opening this memo does not use

units.rhetorical_move: sets good shape against beyond saving
units.function: define the two ends of the proxy for the council

original_instantiations: Flourishing is one end and a borrowed count is the other.

units.source_excerpt: We characterize the marine environment to be in good shape when the overall seabird population is flourishing. Likewise, we characterize the marine environment to be beyond saving once the seabird population dips below 2500

units.rhetorical_move: names what could speed or slow the timeline

units.source_excerpt: The projected timeline can be accelerated if new technology is developed that allows us to clean up plastic waste more rapidly.
units.reusable_pattern: End the memo on what would shorten the timeline and what would lengthen it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not turn the conditional into a promised date
